one_month_reasoning: Window 2026-10-05 to 2026-11-04 has no Oracle earnings: Q2 FY27 is set for 2026-12-14, outside it. In the window: (1) the $0.50 dividend (record date Oct 9, paid Oct 23 per the Q1 release), which lowers the median by about $0.50; (2) Oracle's Investor Day, which management said on the Q1 call is 'coming up in October' and is likely held at AI World (Las Vegas, Oct 25-28). It is a guidance-type event (FCF-turn date, AI-infrastructure gross margins, possibly FY28 capex or FY30 targets) and could move the stock either way: an FCF date would help, a bigger capex number with no FCF date would hurt; (3) Big-4 hyperscaler Q3 reports in late October with first 2027 capex guides. Our standing capex file says 2026 guides were only ever raised, a slight positive read-through for AI-infrastructure names; (4) FOMC Oct 27-28. The small positive capex tilt roughly offsets the dividend, so the median is ~$143.3. I widen monthly sigma from 16.0% (56%/3.5) to 17% for the Investor Day event. Lognormal, so P(>=spot) ~0.50.

fair_value.method: Blend of 12-month-forward P/E (NTM non-GAAP EPS at Oct-2027 = 8/12 FY28 $11.00 + 4/12 FY29 ~$15.45 = $12.48, less 15% = $10.61, x 15x = $159; weight 0.6) and EV/EBITDA (NTM EBITDA $85.6B less 15% = $72.7B x 8.5x = $618B, less ~$135B Oct-2027 net debt excluding operating leases, over 3.12B shares = $155; weight 0.4). Blend $157.5, rounded to $157.

bear.story: AI-capex digestion, or OpenAI defers or renegotiates part of its ~$300B commitment (about half of RPO). A 2027 recession (Kalshi 21%) tightens financing. Moody's cuts to Baa3 and S&P puts the BBB- on negative outlook. FY28 EPS is revised to ~$8-9, the stock trades ~10x, and the Jan-May 2027 raise is mostly equity.

base.story: OCI grows >65%, FY27 lands at ~$90B revenue, and FY28 EPS comes in ~10-15% below today's $11.00. FCF stays negative but net capex is capped at <=$70B through prepayments and bring-your-own hardware. The rating holds at BBB-/Baa2-3. The stock trades at ~15x NTM non-GAAP (~$10.6), i.e. the fair value.

bull.story: Investor Day or FY28 guidance gives an FCF-positive date, AI-infrastructure margins hold, RPO converts on schedule, and an OpenAI raise or IPO (Kalshi ~50% announcement odds by Jun-2027) clears the counterparty worry. The stock re-rates toward ~19-20x NTM (~$12 EPS), still below the peer median, like META's 2023 recovery after a capex scare.

Fiscal years are calendarised: MSFT 1/2 FY27 + 1/2 FY28 (June FY); CRM and WDAY FY ending Jan-28; ADBE FY ending Nov-27. Range 8.5x (ADBE) to 27.0x (NOW); median 21.7x (21.5x/21.8x midpoint); hyperscaler sub-median ~23.7x, enterprise-software sub-median ~15.5x. ORCL CY27 = 5/12 x $8.14 + 7/12 x $11.00 = $9.81, so 14.6x. comps_summary.our_multiple_vs_peers: 15x NTM non-GAAP at horizon: inside the peer range, ~31% below the 21.7x median, in line with the CRM/WDAY/IBM cluster (14.2-16.7x) and above ADBE. 8.5x forward EV/EBITDA vs ORCL's own ~8.1x CY27 today on a lease-consistent EV.
comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: The discount persists through Oct-2027 on checkable company facts, not sell-side calls: (1) management calls FY27-28 the peak capex years and gives no FCF-positive date; consensus FCF is negative through FY28 and S&P projects FY27 FOCF ~-$42B, whereas every hyperscaler peer funds capex from FCF. (2) Credit: S&P BBB- (one notch above junk) and Moody's Baa2 negative vs A-or-better peers. The base rate for a BBB- issuer to be cut to junk within a year is ~9% (S&P), and I put Oracle at ~10-15% given record CDS. (3) Concentration: ~half of $664B RPO with OpenAI. (4) Earnings quality: non-GAAP EPS is ~23% above GAAP (Q1 $1.92 vs $1.56), while the hyperscaler half of the set reports near-GAAP. Base rate from my lane: ORCL's own 10-year P/E floor is 14.4x TTM, and META in 2022 bottomed ~9x before re-rating only once FCF visibility returned. The discount is not deeper because ORCL has the fastest EPS growth in the set (FY28 +35%) and $664B of contracted backlog.

thesis_break_reason: $105 is ~8% below the 52-week low ($114.50) and is ~10.7x CY27 non-GAAP EPS, ~9.9x the haircut NTM, and ~7x EV/CY27 EBITDA. Trading there would most likely mean a fundamental break: an OpenAI contract cut or deferral, a cut to high yield (base rate ~9-15% a year from BBB-), or failure of the prepay/BYO-hardware model forcing much larger equity issuance. Ordinary 56%-vol noise is not enough. I keep $105 rather than ~$100 because a sustained trade below the 52-week low on these multiples would already price a junk-rating outcome.

reasoning: Anchor: ORCL is down ~51% in a year with 56% realised vol, after a 2024-25 re-rating above 30x on OpenAI-driven RPO. Base rates: the Counterpoint drawdown study gives high median recoveries but is measured from troughs, so it only offsets 12-month loser momentum, for a roughly neutral-to-slightly-positive drift. Analogs: META 2022-23 recovered once FCF stayed positive, while 2001 telecom builders dependent on vendor financing kept falling. Oracle sits between: contracted revenue ($664B RPO, OCI +121%) but negative FCF and rising leverage. Round-2 corrections from the supervisor, each verified: NTM weights are 8/12 FY28 + 4/12 FY29 (NTM $12.48, not $12.97); horizon net debt excludes operating leases and is ~$135-143B at Oct-2027 (Q1 balance sheet re-read: notes $125.3B, cash and securities $37.1B), not the May-2028 $150B; ADBE is 8.5x and CRM 14.3x on Yahoo CY27 (re-fetched), so the peer median is 21.7x on one calendarised basis; S&P is BBB- stable (heise, mlq; one search summary says otherwise, so moderate confidence) and Moody's Baa2 negative. New in-lane base rate: S&P's average one-year downgrade rate from BBB- is ~9.4%, and I put Oracle at 10-15% given record CDS, which trims the credit tail slightly. Kalshi 2027 recession odds are 21% (directly from the API, ~602k volume), below the 23-34% I cited from a search summary in round 1. Fair value $157 (P/E $159 x 0.6, EV/EBITDA $155 x 0.4). Scenarios 28% $90 / 47% $157 / 25% $235 give a mean of $157.7, which reconciles with the $157 fair value. The ladder averages that three-lognormal mixture (sigmas 0.30/0.22/0.25) with a single lognormal (median $142, sigma 0.48, reflecting 56% realised vol and loser momentum); the blend's mean is ~$158.5, about $1.5 above fair value, which is within rounding and the ~$2 of dividends. P(>=spot) is 0.535, down from 0.56. Research was limited: stockanalysis was blocked (Cloudflare) this round, so peer EV/EBITDA stays TTM from round 1.
